thesis.title: How I turn AI technology into enterprise value

stages.title: Find an expensive or constrained workflow
stages.question: What is the most painful manual process in this business?
stages.method: Stakeholder interviews, process observation, workload analysis, and pain-point mapping to identify workflows where time cost, error rate, or capacity constraint is highest.
stages.example: Non-financial-risk workflows—RCSA, TPRM, control testing—typically involve high analyst time, document fragmentation, and repetitive evidence gathering across multiple systems.

stages.title: Identify buyer, process owner, decision chain
stages.question: Who owns this problem and controls the budget?
stages.method: Stakeholder mapping from executive sponsor to process owner to technology gatekeeper. Identifying where purchasing authority sits and how transformation budget is released.
stages.output: Ideal customer profile and qualification criteria
stages.example: CRO, COO, or Head of NFR typically sponsors; risk technology or operations owns delivery; CIO controls integration budget. All three must be aligned.

stages.title: Establish economic and operational baseline
stages.question: What does this cost today in time, effort, and risk?
stages.method: Baseline measurement of analyst hours, cycle times, error rates, and downstream rework. Translate into a business case framing that connects current cost to investment threshold.
stages.example: A DORA evidence-generation cycle that takes weeks and multiple analysts has a measurable baseline—and a clear value proposition for automation.

stages.title: Design and build a credible technical proof
stages.question: Can a working demonstrator validate the hypothesis?
stages.method: Rapid prototype of the core workflow using realistic synthetic data. Focus on the hardest part of the problem—agent orchestration, document extraction, integration handoff—not the easy parts.
stages.example: The public NFR agent platform and DORA control-line builds demonstrate this pattern: real agent orchestration, real integration patterns, real human-approval gates.

stages.title: Integrate enterprise systems and human controls
stages.question: Where does data come from and where do humans stay in control?
stages.method: Map data flows from source systems (GRC, service management, document stores) through agent processing to write-back destinations. Design human approval gates at every consequential decision.
stages.example: Enterprise patterns include ServiceNow integration, Teams/Power Automate approval flows, policy-engine verification, and audit evidence generation.

stages.title: Measure, package, and expand
stages.question: What metrics prove value, and how do we replicate this?
stages.method: Define success metrics before deployment. Measure cycle-time, analyst effort, output acceptance rate, and human-override rate. Package the pattern into a reusable architecture and commercial template.
stages.output: Metrics dashboard, reference architecture, and expansion playbook
stages.example: A single paid design partnership produces baselines, an integrated demonstrator, a production roadmap, and a reusable template for the next workflow or client.

projects.title: Enterprise NFR Agent Platform
projects.problem: Non-financial-risk work is fragmented across service-management records, controls, policies, regulatory information, documents, and manual analyst workflows.
projects.summary: An enterprise-oriented platform combining multiple specialized agent workflows, a knowledge graph, document intelligence, regulatory analysis, human approvals, enterprise integration patterns, and an MCP layer.
projects.commercial: Shows how isolated AI use cases can become a reusable platform and expansion path rather than a collection of disconnected pilots.
projects.diagram: Systems of record → documents & data → knowledge graph → agent orchestration → human approval → enterprise write-back
projects.limitations: Synthetic demonstration · no client data · not a production deployment
projects.caseStudy: The platform demonstrates a full enterprise AI stack: specialized agents handle different NFR domains (RCSA, TPRM, regulatory change), a knowledge graph maintains relationships between controls, policies, and obligations, document intelligence processes unstructured content, and human approval gates ensure consequential decisions remain under human control. Integration patterns reflect real enterprise environments (ServiceNow, Teams, Power Automate) without using any client credentials or data.

projects.title: DORA Article 12 Control Line
projects.problem: Regulatory change is commonly translated manually through policy, controls, infrastructure, verification, documentation, and audit evidence.
projects.summary: A staged workflow connecting a regulatory requirement to control updates, infrastructure proposals, policy verification, compliance documentation, human approval, and an evidence chain.
projects.commercial: Turns an abstract regulatory requirement into a bounded, measurable workflow suitable for a paid design partnership.
projects.diagram: Regulation → guideline → control → infrastructure change → verification → compliance work product → documentation → evidence
projects.limitations: Synthetic demonstration · any efficiency estimate is illustrative, not a measured client result
projects.caseStudy: Starting from a DORA Article 12 requirement, the workflow automatically generates control recommendations, proposes infrastructure changes, verifies alignment against existing policy, produces compliance documentation, routes for human approval, and assembles an evidence package. The state machine ensures traceability at every step. AI provider is abstracted so the same workflow runs against different models. Tests cover the full workflow including edge cases and human-override paths.

projects.title: Enterprise AI Economics Simulator
projects.problem: Enterprise buyers struggle to connect model usage, hosting, shared-platform costs, governance, and expected gains to an all-in AI business case.
projects.summary: An interactive cost and scenario tool for estimating the economics of a shared enterprise AI platform, covering industry assumptions, model routing, cloud/sovereign/on-premise scenarios, and cost-vs-gain projections.
projects.commercial: Demonstrates the ability to translate technical architecture into buyer-facing economics and proposal content.
projects.diagram: Model selection → usage assumptions → hosting scenario → shared platform costs → governance overhead → net economics
projects.limitations: All prices, benchmarks, gains, and allocation values are illustrative planning assumptions.
projects.caseStudy: The simulator allows an enterprise buyer or solution architect to model the full economics of an AI platform investment: model selection and routing strategy, token-cost estimates, cloud vs. sovereign vs. on-premise hosting, shared infrastructure amortization, governance overhead, and projected value gains. Outputs are scenario-comparable, exportable, and designed to support executive decision-making and proposal development.

projects.title: Interactive Personal Story
projects.problem: Translating a personal narrative into an engaging, accessible single-page experience.
projects.summary: An interactive single-page experience combining personal storytelling, data visualization, accessibility, and lightweight product design.
projects.commercial: Demonstrates product thinking, design sensibility, and the ability to work across the full stack independently.
projects.diagram: Content design → visual layout → interaction design → accessibility → deployment
projects.caseStudy: A personal side project exploring the intersection of storytelling and product design. Built entirely in vanilla web technologies with attention to accessibility, motion, and visual hierarchy. Demonstrates independent product thinking outside of an enterprise context.
